label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents a psychologically resilient group characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging only 0.81, PHQ-9 depression scores at 0.31, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near floor at 0.04, these respondents demonstrate strong mental well-being across all three measured dimensions. The profile is anchored by highly educated males with moderate daily screen or internet usage of 1–3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness levels suggesting robust social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology well below clinical thresholds
Near-absent anxiety symptoms indicating strong emotional regulation
Moderate and controlled daily usage patterns (1–3 hours)
Overall psychological profile consistent with high functioning and well-being

label: High-Distress Heavy-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.62), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.65), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.06) all sit in the higher range, indicating a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress across all three domains, with anxiety being the most pronounced.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen time
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Shows the highest distress on anxiety measures (GAD-7 mean ~2.06)
Engages in heavy daily screen use exceeding 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounding psychological burden
tone: Clinically concerned and empathetic; acknowledges significant multi-dimensional distress
